issues.legal_issue: Contempt jurisdiction is not exercised where the alleged conduct causes no real prejudice amounting to substantial interference with the due course of justice.
material_facts: The contempt finding arose from officials forwarding applications concerning a pending proceeding to the magistrate hearing it and seeking his report.
The Court found it was not possible to hold that the forwarding caused prejudice or that action was needed to protect the tribunal.
issues.conclusion: The contempt jurisdiction could not properly be invoked because no real prejudice amounting to substantial interference with the due course of justice was shown; mere impropriety was insufficient.
issues.legal_principle: As stated in Anantalal Singha v. Alfred Henry Watson (1931) 58 Cal. 884 at 895, contempt jurisdiction is not to be invoked unless there is real prejudice that can be regarded as substantial interference with the due course of justice. The court acts for a practical purpose and will not exercise the jurisdiction on a mere question of propriety.

predicates.contempt_proceeding: A court is asked to exercise contempt jurisdiction over alleged conduct connected with a judicial proceeding.
predicates.real_prejudice: The alleged conduct caused actual prejudice to the due course of justice.
predicates.substantial_interference: The alleged conduct substantially interfered with the due course of justice.

issues.definition: When contempt jurisdiction is invoked and the conduct did not both cause real prejudice and substantially interfere with the due course of justice, the jurisdiction is not exercised.

issues.legal_issue: Superior judicial officers do not commit contempt merely by forwarding applications concerning a pending case to the magistrate hearing it and seeking a report in the ordinary discharge of their official duties.
material_facts: The officials were superior to the magistrate hearing a pending proceeding and had supervisory responsibilities concerning his work.
One official forwarded a counter-application received with a recommendation and sought a report; the magistrate advised that a formal complaint be filed, and the official relayed that advice.
The other official forwarded an application containing allegations against the magistrate for his remarks, considered the report, and decided not to withdraw the case.
The applications were transmitted in the usual course of official practice, and the Court found no prejudice or tendency to interfere with the course of justice.
issues.conclusion: The officials’ actions in transmitting the applications and seeking or considering the magistrate’s report did not amount to contempt, and the contempt finding against them was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 3 of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1926, conduct is not contempt merely because an application contains allegations that might relate to the merits of a pending case. The Court held that superior officers could transmit such applications in the ordinary course of supervising a subordinate magistrate. It also relied on section 528 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, which authorized the District Magistrate to withdraw the pending case, and observed that the Code did not prevent facts being brought to the District Magistrate’s attention. The governing threshold was the requirement of real prejudice amounting to substantial interference, as stated in Anantalal Singha v. Alfred Henry Watson (1931) 58 Cal. 884 at 895.

rule.if: appeal_from_contempt_finding and superior_officials and application_concerns_pending_case and application_forwarded_for_report and ordinary_official_duty and no_prejudice

predicates.appeal_from_contempt_finding: The proceeding is an appeal from a finding that conduct connected with a judicial proceeding was contempt.
predicates.superior_officials: The persons who forwarded the application held supervisory positions over the judicial officer hearing the pending case.
predicates.application_concerns_pending_case: The application relates to a case that is pending before the judicial officer.
predicates.application_forwarded_for_report: The officials sent the application to the judicial officer and sought his report or remarks.
predicates.ordinary_official_duty: The officials acted in the ordinary course of supervising the judicial officer or performing their official functions.
predicates.no_prejudice: The forwarding caused no prejudice to the pending proceeding and created no need for action to protect the tribunal.

issues.definition: When superior officials appeal a contempt finding and, in their ordinary official duties, forward an application about a pending case to the officer hearing it for a report without causing prejudice, that forwarding is not contempt.
